capabilities.title: Build a distributed data pipeline: read, transform, write/stream
capabilities.summary: Read Parquet/CSV/JSON/images into a Ray Dataset, transform with vectorized map_batches, and write out or stream batches larger than memory.

when: Processing large datasets (>100GB) for ML training.
Distributed data preprocessing across a cluster is needed.
Data is larger than memory and needs streaming execution.
avoid_when: Small data (<1GB) on a single machine — use pandas.
Tabular data with SQL-like operations — use Dask.
Enterprise ETL and SQL queries — use Spark.

steps: Read data: ray.data.read_parquet/read_csv/read_json/read_images from s3://, gs://, or local paths (Parquet recommended for ML), or from_items/from_pandas for in-memory objects.
Transform with vectorized ds.map_batches(fn, batch_size=...) — prefer it over row-wise ds.map, which is slower.
Filter with ds.filter and aggregate with ds.groupby(...).count()/map_groups as needed (execution is lazy).
Consume: ds.write_parquet/write_csv/write_json for outputs, or stream with ds.iter_batches(batch_size=...) to process data larger than memory.

validation: Output row counts and schema match expectations after transforms.
Bulk transforms use vectorized map_batches, not row-wise map.

capabilities.title: Distributed GPU batch inference with a per-worker model
capabilities.summary: Wrap the model in a callable class that loads once per worker, then map_batches with num_gpus to run inference across the dataset.

when: Running batch inference with a GPU model over a large dataset.
avoid_when: Interactive or low-latency online serving — Ray Data is a batch system.

steps: Define a callable class whose __init__ loads the model (once per worker) and whose __call__ maps a batch to predictions.
Run predictions = ds.map_batches(BatchInference, batch_size=32, num_gpus=1) to request a GPU per worker.

validation: The model is constructed in __init__ (once per worker), not per batch.
The output dataset contains the prediction column for every input row.

capabilities.title: Ray Data performance levers and scaling reference
capabilities.summary: Repartitioning, batch-size tuning, streaming execution, and GPU acceleration numbers for sizing a pipeline.

when: A Ray Data pipeline is slower than expected.
Tuning parallelism or batch size for a cluster.

steps: Repartition to match the cluster: ds.repartition(100) for a 100-core cluster.
Prefer large map_batches batch_size (e.g., 10000 vs 100) — vectorized ops dominate.
Stream with iter_batches instead of materializing when data exceeds memory.
GPU transforms: pass num_gpus=1 to map_batches with a CUDA-using function.
Scaling reference (100GB job): 1 node/16 cores ~30 min; 4 nodes/64 cores ~8 min; 16 nodes/256 cores ~2 min.
GPU image preprocessing reference: ~1,000 img/s CPU-only; ~5,000 img/s 1 GPU; ~18,000 img/s 4 GPUs.

capabilities.title: Feed Ray Data into Ray Train (or PyTorch/TensorFlow loops)
capabilities.summary: Pass datasets into TorchTrainer, shard them to workers via get_dataset_shard, or convert with to_torch/to_tf for framework-native loops.

when: Feeding a Ray Dataset into Ray Train distributed training.
Converting a Ray Dataset into PyTorch or TensorFlow batch iterators.

steps: Pass datasets={'train': ds} to TorchTrainer(train_func, datasets=..., scaling_config=ScalingConfig(num_workers=N, use_gpu=True)).
Inside train_func, obtain the worker's shard: train_ds = ray.train.get_dataset_shard('train').
Alternatively convert directly: ds.to_torch(label_column, batch_size) or ds.to_tf(feature_columns, label_column, batch_size).

validation: train_func receives a dataset shard and yields batches of the expected size.
